_doc: THE REAPER'S LEDGER — what each session left behind, recorded by
the reaper (an external cron) rather than by the session itself.
A dead session cannot run its own close-out. This file is what a
manager arriving COLD reads to learn what a session that is no
⚠️ `no_landing_evidence` IS NOT `lost`. See the state table in
CANNOT see — read it beside `by_state`, never `by_state` alone.

coverage.unregistered_attribution_caveat: A session id recovered here says WHOSE the work is, never WHAT it was for: `owns_object` lives only in the registry, so an unregistered session's work is locatable and still unattached to any work object. Recovery is not a substitute for registering.
coverage.unregistered_caveat: COUNT ONLY, no ratio: `claude/**` includes board-post and relay branches that were never sub-sessions, and the registry began 2026-09-01 while branches predate it. This is an upper bound on unregistered sessions, not a measurement of them.
coverage.unpushed_caveat: Work never pushed lives in a container nothing outside it can reach. The reaper has ZERO visibility of it and no reaper can have any. The only remedy is pushing early.
coverage.liveness_caveat: The reaper cannot tell alive from dead — `list_sessions` is an MCP tool CI does not hold. It grades branch quiescence, a PROXY, which is safe only because it records and never acts.
